title: Enzymes
examples: How does an enzyme speed up a reaction?
What happens to enzymes if they get too hot?
Does the shape of the enzyme change with pH?

explain.say: Enzymes are biological catalysts found in living things. They speed up chemical reactions in your body.
The lock and key model suggests the enzyme fits its substrate perfectly. Think of a specific key fitting a specific lock.

draw.text: Lock and Key Model: Specific fit.

explain.say: A more modern idea is the induced fit model. The enzyme changes shape slightly when the substrate enters. This makes the fit even better.

draw.text: Induced Fit: Shape changes upon binding.

explain.say: Temperature affects enzyme activity greatly. Enzymes work best at an optimum temperature, usually near body temperature.
pH levels also control enzyme function. Enzymes have an optimum pH where they work most effectively. Stomach acid has a very different pH.
In real life, your stomach uses enzymes that only work well in a highly acidic environment. This keeps the enzymes safe from the harsh acid.

faq.q: Do enzymes use up the substrate?
faq.a: No, enzymes are catalysts. They speed up the reaction but are not used up themselves in the process.
asks: Are enzymes consumed in the reaction?

faq.q: What happens if the temperature is too low?
faq.a: If the temperature is too low, the enzyme slows down but it is not permanently damaged. It can resume working when warmed up.
asks: Can enzymes work in the cold?

faq.q: What does 'denature' mean for an enzyme?
faq.a: Denaturation means the enzyme loses its specific three-dimensional shape. This loss of shape means it can no longer bind to its substrate.
asks: How is an enzyme permanently damaged?

faq.q: Is the active site the same as the substrate?
faq.a: No, the active site is the specific pocket on the enzyme. The substrate is the molecule that the enzyme acts upon.
asks: What is the difference between enzyme and active site?

faq.q: Do all enzymes have an optimum pH?
faq.a: Yes, most enzymes have a specific optimum pH range. This is because their structure depends on the hydrogen ion concentration.
asks: Why is pH important for enzymes?

facts: Enzymes are proteins that act as biological catalysts.
The active site is where the enzyme binds to the substrate.
High temperatures can cause enzymes to denature permanently.
Enzymes have an optimal temperature and pH for maximum activity.

quiz.say: If an enzyme is heated very high, what is the most likely outcome?

options.show: The reaction rate will slow down slowly.
options.say: The reaction rate will slow down slowly.

options.show: The enzyme will lose its specific shape and stop working.
options.say: The enzyme will lose its specific shape and stop working.

options.show: The substrate will also be destroyed.
options.say: The substrate will also be destroyed.

options.show: The enzyme will become more active.
options.say: The enzyme will become more active.

quiz.why: High heat breaks the weak bonds holding the enzyme's 3D structure, changing the active site.

wrong.0: Denaturation is usually a rapid and irreversible process, not a slow slowing.
wrong.2: While the substrate might degrade, the primary effect described is on the enzyme's structure.
wrong.3: Increased heat energy does not increase the efficiency if the structure is damaged.

quiz.say: Which model suggests the enzyme changes shape when the substrate binds?
quiz.why: This model describes the dynamic interaction where the binding causes a slight conformational change.

wrong.1: This model suggests a pre-formed, perfect fit without structural change.
wrong.2: This describes the process, not the binding mechanism.
wrong.3: This is a general concept, not the specific binding model described.

quiz.say: If an enzyme has an optimum pH of seven, what happens if it is placed in a solution with a pH of two?

options.show: The enzyme will speed up its reaction rate.
options.say: The enzyme will speed up its reaction rate.

options.show: The substrate will change its shape to fit.
options.say: The substrate will change its shape to fit.

options.show: The enzyme will only slow down slightly.
options.say: The enzyme will only slow down slightly.

options.show: The enzyme will likely denature or become greatly inactive.
options.say: The enzyme will likely denature or become greatly inactive.

quiz.why: Extreme pH levels disrupt the ionic bonds necessary to maintain the enzyme's correct shape.

wrong.0: Extreme pH levels are too harsh to maintain the necessary structure for catalysis.
wrong.1: The substrate's shape is generally fixed by its chemical structure.
wrong.2: A pH of two is far from optimum and usually causes significant structural damage.
